subtopics.title: Report basics and International Day of Happiness
subtopics.summary: The World Happiness Report is published annually by the Wellbeing Research Centre at the University of Oxford, in collaboration with Gallup and the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network. Participants rate their lives on a scale of 0 to 10, and the report uses six key indicators. The 2026 edition was released on the International Day of Happiness, which is observed on 20 March and coincides with the vernal equinox.
facts: 2026 is the 14th edition of the World Happiness Report
Published annually since 2012
Published by the Wellbeing Research Centre, University of Oxford
Prepared in collaboration with Gallup and UN SDSN
Participants rate their lives on a scale of 0 to 10
Six key indicators: GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity, perception of corruption
Report helps countries assess development beyond GDP
International Day of Happiness observed on 20 March
Day coincides with the vernal equinox
Theme of International Day of Happiness 2026: Care and Share
Day was pioneered by Bhutan, which prioritised Gross National Happiness over GDP

subtopics.title: Global rankings 2026
subtopics.summary: Finland ranked first in the 2026 report, its ninth consecutive year at the top, with Iceland and Denmark following. Costa Rica rose to 4th place from 23rd, while Afghanistan ranked lowest at 147th. No Anglosphere nation appeared in the top 10 for a second consecutive year, which the report links to a shift in global happiness rankings.

Iceland and Denmark follow Finland in the top ranks
Costa Rica: rank 4, moved up from 23rd
Afghanistan: lowest ranked at 147th
Sierra Leone and Malawi follow Afghanistan at the bottom

USA 23rd, Canada 25th, UK 29th

subtopics.title: India and BRICS comparison
subtopics.summary: India ranked 116th in the 2026 report with a score of 4.536, improved from 118th. Its areas of improvement were social support and healthy life expectancy. Among BRICS nations, China ranked highest at 65th, and India ranked below Nepal and Pakistan but above Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.
facts: India: rank 116th, score 4.536
India improved from 118th in the previous ranking
India's areas of improvement: social support and healthy life expectancy
China ranked 65th, the highest among BRICS nations
India ranked below Nepal (99th) and Pakistan (104th)
India ranked above Bangladesh (127th) and Sri Lanka (134th)

subtopics.title: Social media and youth well-being
subtopics.summary: The 2026 report examines how social media use relates to happiness among young people. Youth aged 15 to 24 report lower life satisfaction than those aged 60 and above, a pattern seen in the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. Adolescent girls using social media for more than five hours a day are the most vulnerable group, while youth using it for under one hour a day report the best well-being.
facts: Youth aged 15-24 report lower life satisfaction than elderly aged 60+
Age-based pattern observed in US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand
Most vulnerable group: adolescent girls using social media over 5 hours a day
Heavy use linked with decline in mental health and comparison-driven stress
Optimal threshold: youth using social media under 1 hour a day
Youth using under 1 hour a day report even better well-being than non-users
Digital paradox: in developing countries like India, digital access improves education and connectivity
Excessive use in the same settings causes stress and anxiety
Report provides insights into mental health and digital behaviour trends

quizzes.passage:
The World Happiness Report is an annual ranking of countries based on how people evaluate their own lives. Respondents are asked to rate their lives on a numbered scale, and the results are read together with six key indicators. These indicators are GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity and perception of corruption. Because the report looks at these factors together, it helps countries assess development beyond GDP alone.

The report does not compare countries only on one global list. It also places countries within regional and economic groups, so that a country can be seen against its neighbours and against the other members of BRICS. India is one of the countries studied in South Asia, and its position can be read alongside the positions of its neighbours. Such comparisons show how a country stands relative to others in its own group.

India's place in the 2026 edition can also be compared with its earlier position, because rankings can move from one edition to the next. A change in rank is shown alongside the country's score, so the movement and the level of well-being can be read together. Areas where a country has improved are also identified in the report.

The 2026 report was released on International Day of Happiness, which is observed every year on 20 March. The report emphasises well-being as a policy goal.

quizzes.passage:
The 2026 World Happiness Report examines how social media use relates to happiness among young people. The report looks at life satisfaction across age groups, comparing how people in different age brackets rate their lives. It also considers how much time young people spend on these platforms, rather than treating all use as the same. The study is therefore about patterns of use as well as the simple fact of using these platforms.

Life satisfaction in the report is measured through people's own ratings of their lives, which allows the results to be compared across groups and countries. The age comparisons are drawn from the same survey data that produces the country rankings. The findings are presented as a set of key insights. Some of these insights concern developing countries, where the effects of digital tools are discussed separately.

The report also describes situations in which the same tools bring strain. Its findings suggest that the amount of use matters, since some levels of use are associated with lower well-being than others. Taken together, these insights help show how young people are faring in a digital environment.

The report was released on International Day of Happiness, and it is part of the annual series published under the World Happiness Report name.
